clue.text: See 10
Cricketing references have gone on too long

parts.note: an over is a set of six balls bowled in cricket
a run is the basic unit of scoring in cricket

explanation.surface: Someone complains that the cricket talk has dragged on far too long.
explanation.walkthrough: One phrase gives two cricket words: OVER, a set of six deliveries, and RUN, a point scored.
explanation.definitionFit: To exceed an allotted time is to overrun, as a meeting or broadcast that runs late does.

clue.text: Plant sacrificed, firstly, in blood and guts

indicators.note: the first letter of sacrificed is placed inside the word for blood and guts

parts.note: gore is spilt blood, as in a gory scene

indicators.note: firstly asks for just the opening letter of the word sacrificed

explanation.surface: A gruesome image of a plant offered up amid bloodshed.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorse is a spiny yellow-flowered shrub common on heathland, so it is a plant.

clue.text: Complex woman having to decide on artist

parts.note: to elect is to choose or decide on
RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: A complicated woman who must make up her mind about a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Electra gives her name to the Electra complex, so she is the woman behind a psychological complex.

clue.text: One zooms around black lines on maps

parts.note: the Roman numeral I stands for one

indicators.note: around says the word for zooms surrounds the letter for black

parts.note: to soar is to zoom upwards
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone races around black lines drawn on charts.
explanation.definitionFit: Isobars are the lines on weather charts joining points of equal atmospheric pressure.

clue.text: Homeless snail, perhaps, saving 500 euros, initially, for deposit

indicators.note: saving here means keeping inside, so the slug encloses the numeral

parts.note: a slug is in effect a snail without its shell, its home
D is the Roman numeral for 500

indicators.note: initially takes only the first letter of euros

explanation.surface: A tale of a shell-less snail hoarding cash as a down payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deposit' looks financial beside the euros, but it means a muddy sediment.
explanation.definitionFit: Sludge is thick muddy sediment, the kind of deposit left at the bottom of a tank.

clue.text: Wind that in large intestine gets drier

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the word for the gut

parts.note: the bowel is the large intestine

indicators.note: wind as a verb means twist, so the letters of that are twisted round

explanation.surface: A crude remark about intestinal gas drying someone out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' reads as flatulence beside the intestine, but it is the verb to twist: 'in' places ATHT inside, and 'drier' is a thing that dries, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A bath towel is something you dry yourself with, so it is a drier.

clue.text: Dish best served cold ending in cooker, still, say, rising

indicators.note: ending in takes the last letter of the word cooker

parts.note: even is used as still in 'even better'

indicators.note: rising, in a down clue, means the abbreviation is read upwards

parts.note: eg, for example, is what say means

explanation.surface: A kitchen scene with something left in the cooker, rising.
explanation.walkthrough: EG turned upwards by 'rising' gives GE.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says revenge is a dish best served cold, so the phrase stands for vengeance.

clue.text: Bird taking drug, one entering bay

parts.note: charlie is slang for cocaine
someone who parks a car in a bay is a parker

explanation.surface: A bird on drugs fluttering into a bay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird' is not a feathered creature but the nickname of the jazz saxophonist.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlie Parker, the bebop saxophonist, was universally nicknamed Bird.

clue.text: Ask about ugly monster lying back, legs buckling — what made her appear beautiful?

indicators.note: about says the word for ask goes round the turned monster

parts.note: to beg is to ask

indicators.note: lying back says the monster's name reads backwards

parts.note: an ogre is an ugly monster of fairy tales

indicators.note: buckling legs collapse, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone tells of an ugly monster sprawled backwards, legs giving way, and wonders why she seemed lovely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lying back' turns the monster round, 'about' wraps the word for ask around it, and 'buckling' jumbles the legs. The definition is a question because the slang names the cause of misjudged beauty.
explanation.definitionFit: Beer goggles is slang for the drunken illusion that makes someone look more attractive than sober eyes would judge.

clue.text: Old queen's domicile hosting opera, not opening, as full

parts.note: ex means former or old

indicators.note: hosting means holding a guest within, so the home encloses the opera

parts.note: a queen bee lives in a hive

indicators.note: not opening means the opera loses its first letter

parts.note: Faust is an opera by Gounod

explanation.surface: An elderly queen's home stages a performance, though not from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: The queen is a bee, not a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Exhaustive means thorough and complete, covering everything, so a full account.

clue.text: Hot office aboard craft

indicators.note: aboard means on board, inside the craft

parts.note: art is a skill or craft
a den is a private study or office

explanation.surface: An office working on board a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' suggests a vessel, but it means skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardent means burning, from Latin ardere, and so passionate or literally hot.

clue.text: See 27
See 17
Dish of the type mentioned earlier, including fishy tacos

indicators.note: including says the word for of that type holds the jumbled letters

parts.note: such refers back to a type already named

indicators.note: fishy means suspicious or odd, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A recipe note on a dish of that sort, made with fish tacos.
explanation.definitionFit: Succotash is an American dish of sweetcorn and lima beans.

clue.text: Spotted dick, perhaps — charming!

definitions.meaning: spotted dick is a British steamed suet pudding with currants, an example of a dessert
an exclamation meaning delightful or lovely

explanation.walkthrough: Spotted dick is a British steamed suet pudding studded with currants; in Britain a pudding course is called a sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet is a British word for dessert, and sweet also means delightful or charming.

clue.text: Interpose uninvited and get involved in a row?

definitions.meaning: to butt into others' affairs without being asked
literally to put a paddle into the water while rowing

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is literal: a rower helping in a row puts an oar into the water.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to meddle, and taken literally describes joining in with rowing.

clue.text: Server, one used to 26 fish!

parts.note: a teat is what a baby feeds from, as in the answer to 26
the ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: A waiter who feeds a baby and also serves fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 26-across is BREASTFEED; a TEAT is used for that.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea tray serves drinks and cups, so it is a server in the sense of a carrying dish.

clue.text: Tongues entwined, splashing around

indicators.note: around here means messed about, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A kissing couple splashing about in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tongues entwined' suggests a kiss, but tongues are languages.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanglish is a hybrid of Spanish and English, two languages woven together.

clue.text: Statesman Cameron casually held up by granny

indicators.note: held means the grandmother's word keeps the other inside

parts.note: nan is an informal word for grandmother

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the name is read from the bottom

parts.note: Dave is the casual form of David, as in former prime minister David Cameron

explanation.surface: A politician named Cameron delayed by his grandmother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Statesman' suggests a politician, but means a man from a US state; DAVE turned upwards gives EVAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nevadan is a native of Nevada, so literally a man of a state.

clue.text: Pleasure's up, suitable to hop the twig

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: fun's, the possessive of fun, gives pleasure
fit means suitable

explanation.surface: Pleasure is rising, fit for an old-fashioned way of dying.
explanation.walkthrough: FUNS turned upwards gives SNUF. 'Hop the twig' is British slang for dying.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are slang euphemisms for dying.

clue.text: See 27
Wrecker has to be composed, piercing old reptile's tail?

indicators.note: piercing means the anagram goes through the middle of the ending

parts.note: -saur is the end of dinosaur, the old reptile

indicators.note: composed means put together, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A destroyer stays calm while spearing a dinosaur's tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' scrambles TO BE into BOTE; the tail is the end of the word dinosaur, not of the creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A saboteur deliberately wrecks or damages things.

clue.text: Bloody beautiful woman secures ring

indicators.note: secures means holds firmly within, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: Venus, the goddess of love, stands for a beauty
O looks like a ring

explanation.surface: A gorgeous woman gets hold of a ring, bloody marvellous.
explanation.definitionFit: Venous means relating to the veins and the blood they carry.

clue.text: Penned by Delany, Longfellow's material

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed by the following words, which hold the answer

explanation.surface: A note that something was written by Delany and by Longfellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penned' looks like writing but means enclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylon is a synthetic fabric, a material.

clue.text: Bear a child consuming large meal, female on the end?

definitions.text: Bear a child consuming large meal, female on the end?

indicators.note: consuming means swallowing, so one word holds the other

parts.note: to breed is to produce offspring

indicators.note: on the end says the letter for female shifts to the last place

parts.note: a feast is a large meal

explanation.surface: A mother has a baby and takes a huge meal, the baby feeding last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the end' makes EASTF and 'consuming' sets it inside; read whole, the clue also describes a mother feeding her baby, the question mark flagging the double reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A mother who has borne a child and nourishes it at the breast is nursing it.

clue.text: Politics all over the place?

definitions.meaning: the three main points on the political spectrum

explanation.walkthrough: The political spectrum's three positions double as an idiom for everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means everywhere, and literally names the three positions on the political spectrum.

clue.text: It's hard in schools to find exotic fruits

indicators.note: in says the letter goes inside the word for schools

parts.note: lycées are French secondary schools
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Fruits from abroad are hard to come by in schools.
explanation.definitionFit: Lychees are small sweet fruits from China with rough red skins.

clue.text: Silliness in a fool, stupidity ultimately

parts.note: a nit is a fool, short for nitwit

indicators.note: ultimately takes the final letter of stupidity

explanation.surface: Foolishness found in an idiot, stupidity at last.
explanation.definitionFit: Inanity is pointless foolishness, silliness.
